title: Filtered continuity of constant abelian higher direct images at coefficient size
statement: Let $h:Y\to X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes in universe $u$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $q\in\mathbf N$ and let $I$ be a filtered category in $\operatorname{Type}(u+1)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The functor from abelian groups in that universe to abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] sending $A$ to $R^q h_*\underline A$ preserves colimits of shape $I$. Here $\underline A$ is the constant abelian sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and the higher image is the degree-q homology of the bounded-below derived direct image of $\underline A$ placed in degree zero [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Preservation is for the cocone with the original mapped coprojections; no torsion assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03Q5 (lemma-colimit), Tag 0739 (lemma-colim-works-over-collection), and Tag 03Q8 (lemma-higher-direct-images); filtered-union step 2 of lem-sbc-constant-module-higher-direct-image-cyclic-reduction.

proof.text: Define the coefficient functor P_hq using the actual shifted preadditive Yoneda functor and restriction along the free represented sheaf functor. Restrict it to the affine etale site. On each affine object U its pullback V=U times_X Y is qcqs by permanence of h.

The coefficient-natural raw evaluation isomorphism identifies P_hq evaluated at U with inverse image to V followed by ordinary derived cohomology in degree q. Inverse image is a left adjoint, so preserves colimits. Apply etaleCohomology_isColimit_large_filtered on V; it retains the original cocone. Pointwise preservation implies preservation by the presheaf functor restricted to the affine site.

Affine-site sheafification preserves colimits. Dense-subsite sheafification compatibility identifies this functor with small-site sheafification followed by restriction. Restriction is an equivalence, and therefore reflects colimits. Hence P_hq followed by small-site sheafification preserves the filtered colimits.

Transport preservation along the coefficient-natural sheafification functor comparison. This gives preservation by the abelian higher-image functor on all coefficient sheaves. Compose with the constant-sheaf functor, a left adjoint. No pullback-constant comparison is needed, since the preceding preservation argument works for all sheaves.

proof_origin.place: Affine-site transport of filtered continuity; coefficient-natural comparison bridges isolated as two proper subarguments.
